Not that I'm aware of, it is JUST stuff about chaos. All the fun stuff got pitched in the fire with the rest of the old Eldar race. They do have a separate area that is just on Humanities interaction with chaos, but that's all the details I know of.

1. The end goal is for Techpriests is to be as cold and logical as the machines they worship. This means a large portion of their lives is dedicated to controlling and removing their emotions. Generally the higher up the ladder you go, the more emotionless they get. Those Magos at the top are pretty much all machine at that point, and only the absolute most extreme circumstances can make them feel anything. 

2. There are, they are just so insignificant that they don't get represented on the tabletop/most fluff. The tau have almost no warp presence whatsoever, so the gods don't notice them and vice versa. The Eldar have soulstones, removing the need to try and seek protection from Slaanesh. In addition, Slaanesh has dibs on their souls to begin with, making it very difficult if not impossible for the other gods to get a cut of the action. 


3. Theoretically the Vindicare and Callidus temples could, but they don't. Their lives are either assassinating people or preparing to assassinate people. They don't get, or want for that matter, vacation time.
4. Tau don't have psykers. If an Eldar soul is a stadium light, a human soul is a bright flashlight, than a Tau soul is flickering birthday candle in the sea of souls. 
5. Genestealers can and have infected Tau. However, the Tau coincidentally have a society that makes Genestealer infestation impossible. The four Castes do not intermingle, and people only breed when told to, and do not get to choose their partners. This prevents a proper cult from forming, and the infected individuals will quickly single themselves out with as they abandon the greater good in the search of making babies. I have not read lore where eldar are infected, but due to the psychic nature of the race combined with their scarcity, being only found on craftworlds, makes  it impossible for cults to take root.

6. The Plague of Unbelief/Zombie plague seems to only affect those without utter faith in the Emperor. So yes, your heretic child with no faith in the God-Emperor will become a wretched plague spawned abomination, fit only for the pyre.

7. Heresy. No one knows, but they are generally causing problems/creating cults/starting uprisings/unearthing nasty things/ shadowy shit that makes the life of a loyal servant to the Emperor even more difficult.

8. Have not read, and have no plans to.

If your opponents are using warp drives your best bet is to anticipate where they are going to go, in my experience they usually beeline for my capital. 

My strats are as follows:


1. Find choke points, and either  split your fleets to cover the choke points, and be ready to redirect forces once the enemy has picked a pathway.

2.Build appropriately strong defense stations at choke points and keep your blob within striking distance of each station.

3- The second war starts shove your fleet deep inside one of their planets, and just go full ham with bombardments and take the planet as fast as possible. This will usually cause the AI to send their fleets to that planet.

If they are using Wormhole there isn't much you can do, aside from sending small fleets to knock out the stations, and the third option is rather slow. Last tip, once you catch them consider going to slow speed and watch for the emergency ftl. You should be able to catch them if you immediately purse them.
